text:
julia: starting controlled canary for r-2026.04 on textgen-service, shifting 5% now. change window ends 18:00Z. deploy-bot: canary shift initiated -> r-2026.04 @ 5% :rocket;

deploy-bot: shift record:
```
from: 0%
to: 5%
routes: textgen/generate, textgen/chat
regions: us-east, eu-central
ver: r-2026.04
started_at: 2024-03-12T10:05:31Z
```

owen: watching SLO panel: https://grafana.company/redwood/textgen-slos p50/p95/errors. p95 looks stable but error rate on textgen/chat spiked to 0.9% in eu-central in the last 2m. :thinking_face:

maya: getting `2023: grpc: connection reset by peer` traces from the chat backend, sample span: `chat-handler -> token-encoder -> response-serializer`

infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale up triggered for transformer-pool-eu (3 -> 5). reason: CPU pressure 92% across pods.

julia: hold ramp. can we enable per-route circuit-breaker on chat to fallback to r-2026.03? we have route-level fallback support.

deploy-bot: applied circuit-breaker: `rbctl circuit --route textgen/chat --threshold 0.5% --fallback r-2026.03 --duration 300s` by julia at 10:09:12Z

owen: after circuit enabled, external error surface for chat dropped to 0.15% in 3m. internal traces still show a cluster of `batcher stall` messages when payloads >2k tokens.

maya: I pulled a trace with timing: encode 120ms, model-infer 700ms, serialize 90ms. batcher stall logs show `lock wait > 500ms` at batcher-shard-3.

julia: quick check: did we change batcher sync in this release? release-czar: release notes mention a refactor to the batching mutex in r-2026.04 to reduce tail latency. https://github.com/redwood/release-notes/r-2026.04.md

release-czar: note: change also included updated netty pool settings, possible regressions under high concurrency.

infra-bot: node az1-gpu-7 reported oom_kill for sidecar-proxy at 10:07:01Z. kernel log excerpt: `oom_killer: kill process 2345 (istio-proxy)`

owen: possible noisy neighbor + new batcher mutex causing stalls. recommendation: keep canary at 5% but pin `textgen/chat` route to r-2026.03 until we can push a targeted fix.

julia: agree. apply per-route pin. deploy-bot: run `rbctl pin --route textgen/chat --version r-2026.03 --reason "canary chat errors/sidecar oom"`

deploy-bot: route pin success -> textgen/chat pinned to r-2026.03 by julia at 10:12:38Z :white_check_mark:

nowen: telemetry after pin shows request success back to baseline, but internal canary traces still show the batcher stall. I'll open IH ticket and attach traces.

release-czar: we need a decision: revert whole release or ship a narrow patch to batcher mutex and netty pool defaults. what's the estimated blast radius?

julia: blast radius high for chat route, lower for generation-only routes. I want a minimal rollback of chat changes in the artifact and a patch deploy. which is faster?

maya: minimal rollback of chat subsystem would take ~40m including CI, patch ~90m. rollback safer for the rest of the release but still needs validation.

deploy-bot: voting poll started: `rollback-full-release` vs `patch-batcher` (voting window 15m). react with :+1: for rollback, :thumbsup: for patch.

julia: I vote patch (thumbsup).

nowen: vote rollback (:+1:). reasoning: sidecar oom + batcher stalls could hide other regressions.

release-czar: tie-breaker: prefer rollback when customer facing error >0.5% and root cause unclear. chat had 0.9% briefly. I'm leaning rollback.

julia: ok, we revert the chat changes in the release. deploy-bot: execute `rbctl rollback --version r-2026.03 --service textgen --scope route:textgen/chat --reason "canary spike and sidecar OOM"`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated -> scope: textgen/chat -> target ver: r-2026.03 by julia at 10:20:01Z

deploy-bot: rollback log:
```
rollback_id: RB-2026-04-01
route: textgen/chat
from: r-2026.04
to: r-2026.03
started_at: 2024-03-12T10:20:01Z
```

nowen: monitoring shows chat errors fall to 0.18% within 2m. p95 latency recovers.

infra-bot: scheduling node reprovision for az1-gpu-7 and cordon drain for the pod that was OOM killed. ticket INFRA-2201 created.

julia: closing canary for chat route. leaving canary for generate endpoints at 5% for additional validation. follow-up items: IH-1201 (batcher mutex investigation), PERF-1202 (netty defaults audit), INFRA-2201.

release-czar: I'll update the release notes and send a short customer-facing blurb about a targeted rollback for chat to avoid confusing users.

julia: thanks all. will reopen thread if new anomalies surface. end thread. :lock:
